blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — More local government units in Metro Cebu suspended in-person classes on Monday, Oct. 12, after air quality deteriorated to “very unhealthy” levels once again. But this time, local pollutants such as vehicle emissions and industrial pollution, and not the transboundary haze from the raging forest and peat fires in Indonesia’s Kalimantan region, have been identified as the main sources, the Environmental Management Bureau in Central Visayas (EMB-7) said. The air quality index (AQI) in Metro Cebu reached 180 on Sunday, Oct. 11, prompting the suspension of in-person classes and the shift to alternative learning delivery modes, including […]...
